Answer: E
Reason: The first image (3-year-old) shows prominent cystic changes and interstitial thickening predominantly in the upper lobes, while the second image (12-year-old) displays a similar pattern of upper lobe cystic spaces and linear markings that are less severe, consistent with the natural history of conditions like Langerhans cell histiocytosis or cystic fibrosis where findings can stabilize or appear less pronounced relative to lung growth over time.
